title: Ohm's law for part of a circuit — resistance
printed_title: 90. Ohm's law for part of a circuit — resistance

prose.text:
Current and voltage
Electric current is the amount of charge flowing past a place per unit time.
This means how much charge passes the same place in each second.

Charge is a property of matter associated with electric pushes and pulls.
A conductor is a material through which charge can move.

Potential difference, also called voltage, compares the energy transferred per amount of charge between two places.
For the ordinary conductor discussed here, its shape and material condition remain unchanged.

Increasing the voltage across it strengthens the internal electric field and increases the average directed motion of charged particles.
An electric field describes the electric push or pull on charge at each place.
This directed motion is the net drift that carries current, not every particle's irregular microscopic movement.
prose.source_text: **伏安特性** 导体中的电流强度是由它两端的电势差来确定. 电势差越大，导体中的电场强度越大，从而带电粒子所获得的定向运动的速度越大.

prose.text:
A conductor may be a solid, liquid, or gas.
Under specified material and measurement conditions, its current has a particular relationship with the voltage across it.
This relationship is called its current-voltage characteristic.

Measuring current for several applied voltages gives this characteristic.
Changing temperature or other conditions can change the relationship.
Knowing it helps us understand the conductor's behavior in a circuit, a connected arrangement through which charge can flow.
prose.source_text: 对于每个导体(固体、液体和气体)，电流强度与两端的电势差都有一定的关系. 这个关系用所谓导体的伏安特性来表示. 测量不同电压时导体中的电流强度，可以求出这个导体的伏安特性. 在讨论与电流有关的所有现象时，伏安特性的知识起着很重要的作用.

prose.text:
Ohm's law: many metal conductors have a current proportional to voltage when temperature and other relevant conditions remain unchanged.
This is a simple form of the current-voltage characteristic.

Proportional means that multiplying voltage by a factor multiplies current by that same factor.
Some conducting electrolyte solutions also follow this relationship within an appropriate operating range.
An electrolyte carries charge through mobile charged atoms or groups called ions.

The original book credits the German researcher Ohm with first establishing this relationship experimentally for metals.
The relationship is therefore called Ohm's law.
The book recalls an earlier discussion in seventh grade, but the needed meaning is explained here.

Ohm's law does not describe every material or device under every condition.
A temperature change, for example, can change a metal conductor's resistance and its current-voltage relationship.
prose.source_text: **欧姆定律** 金属导体和电解液的伏安特性具有最简单的形式. 德国的学者欧姆第一个建立了金属导体的伏安特性.因此，电流强度与电压的关系式命名为欧姆定律. 在七年级时已经详细地讨论了欧姆定律，但是由于它很重要，所以必须重复讨论.

historical_entities.reason: p0218#4 identifies the historical scientist's country; retain the source identity.
p0218#4 attributes the metal-conductor volt-ampere relation to Ohm, not a fictional person.

prose.text:
In Figure 170, conventional current flows from point 1 toward point 2.
Conventional current uses the direction in which positive charge would move.

The potential difference across this part of the circuit is $V=U_1-U_2$.
Electric potential is electrical potential energy per amount of charge, measured from a chosen reference.
U with its lower numbers labels the potential at the respective endpoints, while V labels their difference.

In this passive conductor, which has no electrical supply inside it, current and the electric field point from left to right.
The left endpoint has higher potential than the right endpoint:
$U_1>U_2$.

The greater-than sign compares the two potentials.
The diagram's single arrow shows conventional current, not individual electron tracks, while the electric field has the same direction in this passive conductor but has no separate arrow.
Electrons in a metal drift opposite to conventional current.
prose.source_text: 在图170所示的一段电路上，电流的方向是从点1到点2. 导体两端的电势差(电压)为$V=U_1-U_2$，因为电流的方向是从左向右，所以，电场的方向也是从左向右，从而$U_1>U_2$.

prose.text: Figure 170
prose.label: 图170

prose.text:
For a uniform ohmic conductor with no supply inside this circuit section, current is proportional to applied voltage while temperature and other conditions remain unchanged.
Ohmic means that this conductor follows Ohm's law in the range being considered.
Uniform means that the relevant material and cross-section do not vary along the section.

The proportionality factor is written $1/R$, where $R$ is the conductor's resistance.
For this ordinary ohmic conductor, the factor is the same when the voltage and current directions are reversed.

$I=\frac{V}{R}.$
(9-3) labels this equation, with I for current, V for voltage, and R for resistance.
Divide voltage by resistance to find current.
prose.source_text: 根据欧姆定律，一段均匀电路中的**电流强度与所加的电****压成正比.** 比例系数与方向无关，用$1/R$表示，式中$R$叫做导体的电阻. 因此，$I=\frac{V}{R}.$　(9-3)

prose.text:
Although Ohm's law has a short expression, a precise experiment can be difficult.
The source suggests that measurement difficulties may help explain why Ohm's work was not immediately accepted.
This is the textbook's possible historical explanation, not an established single cause.

For a metal conductor with small resistance, even a substantial current may correspond to a very small voltage.
The electrometer described in §77 was not sensitive enough to measure such small voltages.

The section mark refers to an earlier numbered section.
An electrometer is an instrument for detecting electrical charge or potential, and sensitivity describes how small a change it can detect.
The experiment needed a more sensitive measuring instrument.
prose.source_text: 欧姆定律的形式很简单，但证明它的正确性是很困难的.或许就是因为这个原因，欧姆的工作没有立即被当时的人们所公认. 问题是在于：甚至当电流强度很大时，一段金属导体的电势差也是很小的，因为导体的电阻很小. 在§77中讲过的静电计不能测量很小的电压，它的灵敏度太小，需要一个非常灵敏的仪器.

historical_entities.reason: p0219#1 discusses the historical reception of Ohm's experimental work.

prose.text:
An instrument that measures voltage is called a voltmeter.
This discussion concerns a moving-pointer voltmeter whose calibrated response uses Ohm's law.
It is not a claim that every modern voltage-measuring instrument operates in exactly this way.
prose.source_text: 常用的测量电压的仪器——伏特计，其原理就是利用了欧姆定律.

prose.text:
An ammeter measures current.
In the pointer instrument described here, current through the instrument determines how far its pointer turns.
The voltmeter uses a related mechanism.

When the voltmeter is connected between two circuit points, their voltage determines the small current through it.
Knowing the instrument's resistance allows that current to be used to infer voltage.

Its scale is already marked in volts, so voltage can be read directly.
This description explains the instrument's principle, not instructions for connecting a meter to a household outlet.
prose.source_text: 伏特计的结构原理跟安培计一样. 通过伏特计的电流强度是由接入电路的两点之间的电压来确定. 因此，知道伏特计的电阻时，可以根据电流强度测定出电压. 实际上，仪器的刻度是直接指出电压的伏特数.

prose.text:
Resistance describes how strongly a conductor opposes current under specified conditions.
For an ohmic conductor at a given voltage, greater resistance means smaller current.
From Ohm's law (9-3), when current is not zero, its resistance is $R=\frac{V}{I}$.

The fraction says to divide voltage by current.
Finding resistance in this way requires measuring both the voltage across the conductor and the current through it under the same conditions.
It is not a measurement procedure for a live household circuit.
prose.source_text: **电阻** 电阻是导体的基本电性质. 当给定电压时，导体中的电流强度由这个量来决定. 导体的电阻好象是导体阻碍在其中产生电流的本领的量度. 利用欧姆定律(9-3)，可以测定导体的电阻$R=\frac{V}{I}$. 为此，需要测量电压和电流强度.

prose.text:
G. S. Ohm (1789-1854) was a German physicist who also taught in a secondary school.
He established a current-voltage law for part of a circuit and a law for determining current in a complete circuit.
The book's registered correction to his birth year is retained here; the original source wording remains in the source record.

For his experiments he overcame substantial difficulties and made a sensitive instrument for measuring current.
He used a thermocouple as a supply.

Such a device uses two different metals joined at a junction.
Its voltage depends on that junction's temperature compared with a reference junction in the measurement circuit.

The book describes Ohm increasing this temperature difference to change the voltage.
The voltage is approximately proportional to the difference only over a limited range where the voltage change per degree stays nearly constant.
Ohm also investigated the dependence of resistance on conductor length and cross-sectional area.
prose.label: 欧姆
prose.source_text: G. S. 欧姆(1787～1854)——杰出的德国物理学家，中学教师. 他发现了部分电路上电流强度和电压的关系的定律，以及在全电路中确定电流强度的定律.为此，他克服了很大的困难，制成了测量电流强度的灵敏仪器. 欧姆利用热电偶(两根不同金属焊在一起的导体)作为电源. 欧姆用增大焊点的温度差来改变电压(电压与温度差成正比). 此外，欧姆还发现了电阻与导体的长度及其横截面积的关系.

numeric_changes.reason: SCI90-01: correct the source's historical birth year using Deutsches Museum's first-party Nachlass Georg Simon Ohm (1789-1854), collection NL 267, https://digital.deutsches-museum.de/item/NL-267. Faithful source_text and source pages remain unchanged; this is not a mathematical erratum.

historical_entities.reason: p0219#6 is the biography caption belonging to the unnumbered portrait tbl-p0219-01; preserve the printed initials, name and identity.
p0219#6 identifies Ohm as a German physicist and schoolteacher.

prose.text:
Resistance depends on the material and the conductor's dimensions.
For a uniform material with constant cross-sectional area, a specified temperature and state, and current along its length, let the length be $l$ and the cross-sectional area be $S$.

Cross-sectional area is the size of the face obtained by cutting across the conductor.
Its resistance is:
$R=\rho\frac{l}{S}$.

Here the expression says to multiply the material's resistivity by length and divide by cross-sectional area.
For the same material and conditions, a longer conductor has more resistance, while a larger cross-sectional area gives less resistance.
prose.source_text: 电阻与导体的材料及其几何大小有关. 对于长为$l$、横截面积为$S$的导体，其电阻为$R=\rho\frac{l}{S}$.

prose.text:
The symbol $\rho$, the Greek letter rho, labels resistivity.
Resistivity is a property of the material in a specified state, especially at a specified temperature.
Resistance belongs to a particular conductor, so it also depends on that conductor's shape and size.

To understand the numerical comparison in the International System of Units (SI), imagine a cube of uniform material with every edge $1$ metre long.
Current passes perpendicular to two opposite faces, directly across the cube.

Resistivity measured in ohm-metres has the same numerical value as this cube's resistance measured in ohms.
Equal numerical values here do not make resistance and resistivity the same physical quantity or give them the same unit.
prose.source_text: 这里$\rho$——与物质的种类和物质的状态(首先决定于温度)有关的量. 这个量叫做导体的**电阻率**. 如果电流是沿着正立方体两个对面的法线方向流动，则在国际单位制中，电阻率的数值等于每边长为$1$米的正立方体导体的电阻.

prose.text:
The unit of resistance is the ohm.
If a voltage of $1$ volt produces a current of $1$ ampere through a conductor, its resistance is $1$ ohm.

A volt is a unit of potential difference, and an ampere is a unit of current.
The unit's name honors Ohm.
prose.source_text: 导体的电阻单位是根据欧姆定律建立的，因此叫做欧姆.**如果当电势差为$1$伏特时在导体中形成的电流为$1$安培，则****导体的电阻为$1$欧姆**.

prose.text:
The unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre.
Under ordinary specified conditions, good metals have small resistivity, whereas typical dielectric insulating materials have much larger resistivity.

A dielectric is an insulating material whose bound charges can shift slightly in an electric field.
These comparisons do not mean that a material's resistivity is unchanged at every temperature or operating condition.
prose.source_text: 电阻率的单位是欧姆·米. 金属的电阻率很小. 电介质的电阻率很大.

prose.text:
The original book has an appendix table listing resistivities of some materials.
Such a value must be used with the material and conditions to which it applies, not as an exact unchanging number for every sample.
prose.source_text: 在书末的附表中，列举了一些物质的电阻率的数值.

prose.text:
Why Ohm's law matters: knowing voltage and resistance allows current to be found where Ohm's law applies.
Current can cause heating, chemical changes, and magnetic effects. Calculating those effects also requires their own relevant physical relationships.

A short circuit can occur when a very low-resistance path directly connects supply terminals and bypasses the intended load.
The load is the device intended to use the supplied electrical energy.
In a lighting circuit this can produce a dangerously large current, as indicated by equation (9-3).

Actual current is also limited by the supply and the rest of the circuit, so it is not infinite.
Nevertheless, overheating, fire, or injury can result.
This explains a hazard, so never deliberately short-circuit a supply or experiment with household wiring.
prose.source_text: **欧姆定律的意义** 欧姆定律的实际意义是很大的.当给定电压和已知电阻时，用这个定律可以确定电路中的电流强度. 同时，用它还可以计算电流的热效应、化学效应和磁效应，因为这些效应与电流强度有关. 从欧姆定律可以得出：用电阻很小的导体接通照明电路是很危险的. 根据(9-3)式，电流强度是相当大的，这可能产生严重的后果.

prose.text: **伏安特性** 导体中的电流强度是由它两端的电势差来确定. 电势差越大，导体中的电场强度越大，从而带电粒子所获得的定向运动的速度越大.
对于每个导体(固体、液体和气体)，电流强度与两端的电势差都有一定的关系. 这个关系用所谓导体的伏安特性来表示. 测量不同电压时导体中的电流强度，可以求出这个导体的伏安特性. 在讨论与电流有关的所有现象时，伏安特性的知识起着很重要的作用.
**欧姆定律** 金属导体和电解液的伏安特性具有最简单的形式. 德国的学者欧姆第一个建立了金属导体的伏安特性.因此，电流强度与电压的关系式命名为欧姆定律. 在七年级时已经详细地讨论了欧姆定律，但是由于它很重要，所以必须重复讨论.
在图170所示的一段电路上，电流的方向是从点1到点2. 导体两端的电势差(电压)为$V=U_1-U_2$，因为电流的方向是从左向右，所以，电场的方向也是从左向右，从而$U_1>U_2$.
根据欧姆定律，一段均匀电路中的**电流强度与所加的电****压成正比.** 比例系数与方向无关，用$1/R$表示，式中$R$叫做导体的电阻. 因此，$I=\frac{V}{R}.$　(9-3)
欧姆定律的形式很简单，但证明它的正确性是很困难的.或许就是因为这个原因，欧姆的工作没有立即被当时的人们所公认. 问题是在于：甚至当电流强度很大时，一段金属导体的电势差也是很小的，因为导体的电阻很小. 在§77中讲过的静电计不能测量很小的电压，它的灵敏度太小，需要一个非常灵敏的仪器.
常用的测量电压的仪器——伏特计，其原理就是利用了欧姆定律.
伏特计的结构原理跟安培计一样. 通过伏特计的电流强度是由接入电路的两点之间的电压来确定. 因此，知道伏特计的电阻时，可以根据电流强度测定出电压. 实际上，仪器的刻度是直接指出电压的伏特数.
**电阻** 电阻是导体的基本电性质. 当给定电压时，导体中的电流强度由这个量来决定. 导体的电阻好象是导体阻碍在其中产生电流的本领的量度. 利用欧姆定律(9-3)，可以测定导体的电阻$R=\frac{V}{I}$. 为此，需要测量电压和电流强度.
G. S. 欧姆(1787～1854)——杰出的德国物理学家，中学教师. 他发现了部分电路上电流强度和电压的关系的定律，以及在全电路中确定电流强度的定律.为此，他克服了很大的困难，制成了测量电流强度的灵敏仪器. 欧姆利用热电偶(两根不同金属焊在一起的导体)作为电源. 欧姆用增大焊点的温度差来改变电压(电压与温度差成正比). 此外，欧姆还发现了电阻与导体的长度及其横截面积的关系.
prose.label: 欧姆

prose.text: 电阻与导体的材料及其几何大小有关. 对于长为$l$、横截面积为$S$的导体，其电阻为$R=\rho\frac{l}{S}$.
这里$\rho$——与物质的种类和物质的状态(首先决定于温度)有关的量. 这个量叫做导体的**电阻率**. 如果电流是沿着正立方体两个对面的法线方向流动，则在国际单位制中，电阻率的数值等于每边长为$1$米的正立方体导体的电阻.
导体的电阻单位是根据欧姆定律建立的，因此叫做欧姆.**如果当电势差为$1$伏特时在导体中形成的电流为$1$安培，则****导体的电阻为$1$欧姆**.
电阻率的单位是欧姆·米. 金属的电阻率很小. 电介质的电阻率很大.
在书末的附表中，列举了一些物质的电阻率的数值.
**欧姆定律的意义** 欧姆定律的实际意义是很大的.当给定电压和已知电阻时，用这个定律可以确定电路中的电流强度. 同时，用它还可以计算电流的热效应、化学效应和磁效应，因为这些效应与电流强度有关. 从欧姆定律可以得出：用电阻很小的导体接通照明电路是很危险的. 根据(9-3)式，电流强度是相当大的，这可能产生严重的后果.
